title: Baba Ganoush
subtitle: Smoky charred aubergine dip with tahini
excerpt: Aubergines charred directly over a flame until completely collapsed, then blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic into a smoky, silky dip. The char is where the flavour comes from.

recipe.sourceNotes: Baba ganoush is a Levantine dip made from roasted or charred aubergine, tahini, lemon, and garlic. It is a staple of Lebanese, Syrian, Israeli, and Palestinian cooking. The name translates roughly as 'pampered daddy' in Arabic. The key technique is charring the aubergine directly over a flame, not just roasting it: this creates the smoky flavour that defines the dish. Without the char, it becomes a bland roasted aubergine puree.

content.text: Char the aubergines directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill until the skin is completely blackened and the aubergine has collapsed. This takes 20 to 30 minutes and creates the smokiness the dish depends on. Leave to steam in a colander until cool, then drain off any liquid before blending.

Pierce each aubergine several times with a fork. Place directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill. Cook, turning every 5 to 8 minutes, until the skin is completely blackened all over and the aubergine has completely collapsed, about 20 to 30 minutes.
Place the charred aubergines in a colander. Leave to cool for 15 minutes. Peel away and discard the blackened skin. Drain off any liquid.
Mash or blend the aubergine flesh with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, and salt. Adjust the seasoning. The texture should be slightly rough, not completely smooth.
Spread onto a plate. Drizzle with olive oil, dust with smoked paprika, and scatter with parsley. Serve with flatbread or pitta.
